column1: # Tap manifest for dhtrace. One tap per line, tab-separated:
#   label <TAB> module <TAB> mangled symbol <TAB> json spec
# spec keys:
#   report_arg      register holding a HIDReport reference at function entry
#   returns         "report_array" | "report" | "indirect" — plants a one-shot
#                   breakpoint at LR to capture the result
#   args_are_words  registers to record as plain integers (OptionSet rawValues)
# Breakpoints bind with --skip-prologue false. This is mandatory: the default
# binds past the prologue (measured +32 on a test function, after
# `str x8,[sp,#8]; mov x8,x0`), by which point the argument registers have been
# clobbered. Earlier captures in this repo read arguments at that point and the
# values were not trustworthy.
# --- the transport boundary: every report that reaches the device ----------
# This is the universal tap. It is also the one that sees the AbsolutePointer
# flood, so it relies on the governor to shed itself if Device Hub gets busy.
#send
send_id
# --- lock / unlock: the keyboard filter and the function that builds reports -
# updateCopyMask takes two HIDEventMask values. HIDEventMask is an OptionSet
# over UInt, so both arrive as plain integers, and it returns [HIDReport]
# directly — this is where a key transition becomes wire bytes.
#kbd_copymask
#kbd_filter
#scroll_filter
# Disabled above, with the evidence, rather than deleted:
#   send          the UInt64 overload. Bound, zero hits across a 150 s capture
#                 in which the HIDServiceID overload took 493. DeviceKit uses
#                 the typed one.
#   kbd_copymask  bound, zero hits while Cmd-L was pressed and other taps fired
#                 throughout. updateCopyMask is not on the lock path.
#   kbd_filter    every filter runs for every event (the chain is a reduce over
#   scroll_filter the filter array), so these fire on all traffic regardless of
#                 type and triple the hit rate for attribution the send tap
#                 already provides. They shed at ~31 hits/s each and took the
#                 send tap down with them, voiding the last two windows of the
#                 2026-09-09 capture. Re-enable one at a time when attribution
#                 is the actual question.
